title: Gold & Silver Forecast: Fake-Out or Real Breakdown? + Platinum, Palladium And Copper
speaker: Gareth Soloway

macro_themes.view: Oil +2.1% on the day; with the bond market closed, traders are front-running higher yields by selling gold.
High oil, fuel and rates could deteriorate the global economy, which is bearish for industrial metals (copper, and silver short term).
A trend-line close beyond a level is 50/50; a second close beyond that candle's low/high confirms ~70% of the time.

calls.condition: If gold closes below 4,100 with confirmation, then 3,950 and 3,500
calls.reason: Holding the long-term ascending trend-line support after last week's unconfirmed close below (fake-out). A confirmed close below 4,100 targets 3,950 then 3,500; first resistance is the descending trend line from the all-time high. Holds a small swing long on support, net long long-term; would buy big only near 3,500.
calls.quote: any close with confirmation below 4,100. Then I think we're headed to 3950 and honestly to 3500

calls.condition: If silver breaks the trend line and confirms, then 48-50
calls.reason: Pierced and closed below the long-term trend line without confirming, then got back above; on the sidelines for swing trades (no long, no short) due to oil/rate pressure on the economy. Confirmed collapse targets 48-50 (1980/2011 pivot highs), where he would buy; long-term still bullish.
calls.quote: If silver does collapse and confirms, it's likely going back to about the $50 level.

calls.condition: Bigger drop once the wedge trend line breaks and confirms
calls.reason: Short copper (front-running): ascending wedge with barely-higher highs showing lost strength; a confirmed break of the lower trend line should bring a much bigger drawdown, and a weakening economy hurts a purely industrial metal.
calls.quote: I am short copper. Uh, I love this. This is what we call an ascending wedge pattern.

calls.condition: If the long-term trend line breaks, then ~1,350
calls.reason: Sitting on the long-term trend line inside a tightening band; breakout or breakdown expected within October. A break targets about 1,350.
calls.quote: If this breaks, where are we going? We're likely going back to about 1350 on this chart.

calls.reason: Small swing long off the 0.786 Fibonacci retracement (up a bit), but thinks it goes lower first; a breakdown targets the 0.886 Fib near 1,000 (matching the 2018 low area), his longer-term buy level.
calls.quote: I actually like palladium, but I think it's going to go lower first.

notes: Recorded Monday Oct 12 (bond market closed, oil up ~2.1%). No current prices stated. Gold resistance is a descending trend line from the ATH with no number given. Palladium short-term 'bullish' reflects his small swing long; medium-term bearish reflects 'lower first' to ~1,000.
